note: Look, not law. Absorb or drop next sitting. A spark is not a trap.

items.claim: A control-plane sitting is one class of work; a second class is a split.
items.whyNotLaw: No check yet that a multi-repo transcript fails a sitting.

items.claim: A wall-clock is not a control-plane fuse.
items.whyNotLaw: Named decay signs already cover rot; hours would be an invented clock.
items.because: T25 already names decay signs. A wall-clock would be a second clock.

items.claim: A hosted or private-index code search that returns zero is not a ZERO.
items.whyNotLaw: The search product is not a container. GitHub search of Virbos was empty; the objects were not.

items.claim: A control plane that will issue or drop reads factory/CONTROL_PLANE.md.
items.whyNotLaw: successorReads names sparks but not CONTROL_PLANE.md; CONSOLE does. Drift, not yet a check.

items.claim: An owner paste of a missed spark is a lead, not law.
items.whyNotLaw: No check that a successor treated a chat paste as AGENTS.
items.because: T50 already rules that the repository is the record and a fact from chat or notes is a diary; a second row would be the same law twice.

items.claim: A session that confirms it understands still invents and leaves the loop; reading files or alumni is not a hold.
items.whyNotLaw: Landing checks do not read chat. No command fails a spoken confirmation. Until a return must paste a command or omit, absorbing this is a diary.

items.claim: A return validates spendUsd and cachedTokens and then discards the row, so no command sums spend or cache hits across lanes.
items.whyNotLaw: Returns so far are prose in lane logs; a store with no rows is a fixture, and the cap it would enforce has no dated row in factory/decisions.json.

items.claim: A seat with shell access acts to the limit of the instructions it can read, not the limit of its envelope Holds; a session launched in the control-plane checkout has no Holds at all and will land and push.
items.whyNotLaw: The control plane compares the changed file set to Holds only at the return, after the seat has already acted. No command bounds a running seat, and no check names where a seat may be launched.

items.claim: The spend and cache numbers a return requires already exist in the harness meter, but the seat cannot see them, so spendUsd is self-reported as zero or omitted and factory/returns.json stays empty.
items.whyNotLaw: No command reads a harness meter into a return. Five seat runs produced zero rows, and the reading is the control plane's work, not the seat's.

items.claim: A seat echoes the envelope Runtime stamp as its model: two seats reported deepseek-v4.1-flash while one was in fact running deepseek-flash, so a return's model field records the claim, not the run.
items.whyNotLaw: Nothing records the model the launcher passed, so no check can compare a return's model against it. Until the launcher's pick is written down, absorbing this is a diary.

items.claim: The control plane hands the owner commands in a shell dialect the owner's terminal rejects: PowerShell 5.1 has no && and the parent traps.yaml has no row for the host shell, though Otto's TRAPS.md has carried one since 2026-09.
items.whyNotLaw: No command reads what the control plane types at the owner. The kit's own gate steps run through bash from a file and seat.mjs already prints a Windows variant, so the checkable surface is not obviously the one that failed.

items.claim: alumni.mjs scan measures structure and never opens a child's TRAPS.md, so a lesson a child paid for and wrote down in prose cannot reach the parent by measurement.
items.whyNotLaw: The scan found three structural signals on Otto and missed the shell trap sitting in line 7 of its TRAPS.md. What a portable intake of a prose trap would check is not yet named.

items.claim: The qwen-code seat recipe passes the packet as an argv string, and on Windows a 33 KB packet exceeds the command-line limit: the seat dies with 'Argument list too long' before it reads a byte.
items.whyNotLaw: Observed once on F33's launch. The fix is stdin rather than argv, but no check yet proves a recipe can carry a packet of cap size on the platform the control plane sits on.

items.claim: An issuance commit pushed to main without a skip-ci marker turns the gate red and launches the GHA writer on the lane just issued, onto the same branch a local worktree already holds.
items.whyNotLaw: On F33 the cloud seat started headless with yolo on writer/F33 and was stopped only by a 401 on a stale DashScope secret. The F31 sitting knew this and wrote it as a ledger sentence, not a check.
